stage1.impression: A symmetric, empty, showroom-like frame: a dark, evenly lit procedural drape fills the middle, two red acrylic speakers glow on veneer plinths, and three identical chair backs block the foreground. The speakers' insides read as flat pink signage and the horns sink into black. There is no practical, no pool of light on anything but the plinths, no sign of life, and the wood and felt are smooth CG. A magazine would not publish it as a specific place: it reads as a generic home-theatre or showroom render, with nothing that says a shop that plays records.

blocking_9: The speaker interiors must stop clipping into flat pink (clip_pct under 1 in each speaker region) while the cabinets still glow and stay the brightest colour in the frame
The resin horns must read as tinted, translucent volumes with a highlight along the rim, not near-black slabs (horn region lum_median 20 or more)
The back drape needs a visible wash that falls off from a pool at seat height, plus felt fibre and irregular folds, instead of an even grey of about 25 with a small hotspot at the hem
The frame must show the room as a place: the decks table by the drape, both rows of chairs, the rug, and some sign of a session (a sleeve out, a glass, a coat), at a seated, believable lens
The oak (chairs and plinths) must read as oak, not reddish walnut, and must not repeat one identical grain map on every piece
There must be some atmosphere and some falloff, so the light reads as practicals in a room, not as a studio set

defects.what: Left speaker: the white batts under the 110 W spot go flat salmon pink and clip at 3.29%, so they read as an illuminated sign, not as batts behind thick tinted acrylic
Right speaker: the same flat pink and 3.15% clipping; it is a mirror copy of the left frame
Left horn: crushed to lum_median 10.8 (r 25, g 5), so the tint, the transparency and the edges are lost
Right horn: just as dark and muddy
Back drape: near uniform (lum 15 to 46, falloff bins 20 to 30), with regular, CG-like vertical folds and no fibre; it is a flat dark backdrop
A small isolated light hotspot on the drape's hem (lum 71) that looks like a stray light, not a wash
Centre chair back: a big, blank, smooth veneer slab filling the foreground, reddish (r 59, g 30, b 22); it reads as walnut, not oak
Left chair: the same grain map as the centre chair and the plinths; the seats are flat black with no leather or upholstery texture
Left plinth: smooth CG veneer with a hot top edge (p95 196) and no joinery or end grain
Floor and rug band: smooth and featureless, so the wool rug does not read
A plaster wall corner and a dark rectangle at top right: an unexplained object breaks the drape enclosure
No sign of life, no practical lamp in view, no decks table, perfect bilateral symmetry: a showroom, not a session

changes.problem: The listening pair's spots overexpose the speakers' interiors into flat, clipped pink, which reads as signage.

evidence.measured: clip_pct 3.29, lum_p95 185, flat salmon fill at a 3x crop; right speaker clip_pct 3.15

change.setting: track spots: the listening pair 2 x spot
change.from: 110.0 W, cone 24 deg, aimed at the cabinet's face
change.to: 50 W, cone 30 deg, aimed 0.4 m higher at the horn and the top of the cabinet, so the light grazes the acrylic rather than flooding the batts

changes.expected: The cabinets keep a deep ember glow, the batts read as soft fabric behind tinted acrylic, and the polished edges carry thin highlights; clipping drops below 1%.

changes.problem: The resin horns are crushed to near black, so the hero's silhouette at the top is lost.

change.setting: the listening pair's spots aim, plus the room's fill
change.from: spots at the cabinets; fill 0.05 W/m2
change.to: spots retargeted as in c1 to catch the horn's mouth and rim; fill 0.15 W/m2 at 2900 K

changes.expected: Each horn reads as a translucent ember volume with a lit rim and visible depth, at lum_median 20 to 40.

changes.problem: The back drape is a flat, even grey backdrop, with only a stray hotspot at the hem instead of a wash.

evidence.measured: lum_median 25.6, lum_range 31, falloff bins 20 to 30 top to bottom; isolated hotspot at [560,520,640,580] lum 71

change.setting: soft light: the back felt's wash
change.from: 0.5 W/m2, 2600 K, landing as a hotspot at the hem
change.to: 1.5 W/m2, 2600 K, a wide grazing wash from the ceiling track centred about 1.2 m up the drape, falling off to dark at the top

changes.expected: The folds model in light and shadow, a soft pool sits behind the seats and darkens toward the ceiling, and the hotspot disappears into the pool.

changes.problem: A 22 mm level frame from dead centre behind three chair backs is symmetric, empty and blocked by blank slabs; it shows no decks, no rows and no place.

evidence.measured: a blank chair back fills 23% of the lower frame at lum 36; the frame is mirror-symmetric

change.to: seated in the second row, off axis at about y 2.6, z 1.1, 32 to 35 mm, framed past one chair's shoulder to take in one speaker large and the other smaller, the decks table by the drape, and the front row; f/2.8 focused on the nearer speaker

changes.expected: The frame reads as a specific session room with depth and asymmetry; the hero is read at a glance and the decks give the room its purpose.

changes.problem: There is no sign of life or of a record shop's listening session.

evidence.measured: no glass, sleeve, coat or person in view

change.to: a record sleeve leaning on the decks table with the disc on the platter, a half-full tumbler under a front-row chair, a coat over one chair back, and a session card on one seat

changes.expected: A lived-in, just-paused session; small warm highlights on the glass and vinyl.

changes.problem: The chairs and plinths read as reddish walnut with one repeated, smooth grain map, not as oak.

evidence.measured: r 59 / g 30 / b 22 (r:g about 2:1); the same grain on the left chair and the left plinth

change.from: dark red-brown stain, one grain texture shared by every piece
change.to: a natural or lightly smoked oak with ray fleck, a randomised texture offset and rotation per object, a matte oil sheen (roughness about 0.55), and visible end grain on the plinth tops

changes.expected: The chairs and plinths read as oak furniture, warmer and less red, each piece with its own grain.

changes.problem: The felt and the floor are smooth CG surfaces with no fibre, and the rug does not read.

evidence.measured: even rgb 28/27/27 (delta E 4.3 against #26272A), with regular identical folds; floor band [230,610,970,645] is smooth

change.setting: the felt's finish and the rug
change.from: a smooth charcoal shader with regular folds
change.to: a felt fibre normal and roughness map at real scale (about 1 mm fuzz), irregular fold spacing and slight hem sag; a visible wool rug pile at its edge on the concrete

changes.expected: At 1:1 the drape reads as heavy wool felt and the rug as wool on sealed concrete.

changes.problem: The air is clean and the light has no visible source, so it reads as a studio, not a room lit by practicals.

evidence.measured: no visible beam or practical; upper drape lum_median 24.4 with no gradient from a source

change.to: haze 0.004/m so the listening spots' cones read faintly; seats spot 6 W, so a soft pool lands on the front row; if the plan allows, a Core lamp lit on the decks table

changes.expected: Faint cones from the track down to the speakers, a pool on the seats, and dark between the pools: cozy and low key.

out_of_scope.request: Show the speaker's batts less prominently through the acrylic, or change the Ember tint
out_of_scope.why: The Tropos's shape, colour and parts are fixed; only the light on it can change

out_of_scope.request: Remove one of the two speakers so there is one hero
out_of_scope.why: A pair is the product as placed; the card fixes the Tropos pair on the listening room's plinths

out_of_scope.request: Replace the plain chairs with upholstered or leather lounge seating, or add timber walls or plaster to the drape enclosure
out_of_scope.why: The plan (A-401) fixes the chairs, drapes and their materials

out_of_scope.request: Explain or remove the plaster corner and dark rectangle at the top right
out_of_scope.why: It may be the plan's wall or a back-of-house door; the camera move in c4 should frame it out rather than change the room
